title: GitLab public handbook
text: GitLab, an all-remote company with team members in more than 60 countries, maintains a public company handbook running to thousands of pages that documents its processes, values and remote operating model. Employees are expected to look up and update the handbook rather than rely on ad-hoc guidance.

title: Distributed companies publishing remote-work guidance
text: Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, and Doist, maker of Todoist and Twist, are fully distributed companies that have published written guides on how they work remotely, emphasising asynchronous communication and written documentation over meetings.

title: Share of US workdays worked from home
text: Survey data on US working arrangements shows that roughly a quarter of paid full workdays were worked from home in 2024, down from a peak above 50% in spring 2020 but several times higher than before the pandemic.

title: FDA authorization of AI-enabled medical devices
text: AI-enabled software that meets the definition of a medical device must be authorized by the US FDA before it is marketed, through 510(k) clearance, De Novo classification or premarket approval. In December 2024 the FDA finalized guidance on predetermined change control plans that lets makers pre-specify how an AI model will be updated after authorization.

title: Radiology dominates authorized AI medical devices
text: The FDA's public list of AI-enabled medical devices passed 1,000 authorizations by 2025, and roughly three quarters are in radiology. Typical tools detect findings on chest X-rays, CT scans and mammograms or flag suspected urgent cases, such as brain bleeds, for prioritized review by a radiologist.

title: Pandemic-era surge in telehealth
text: Telehealth use in the US surged during the COVID-19 pandemic. By mid-2021 telehealth utilization had stabilized at about 38 times its pre-pandemic level, and Medicare telehealth visits rose from roughly 840,000 in 2019 to 52.7 million in 2020.

title: WHO guidance on AI ethics in health
text: In June 2021 the World Health Organization published 'Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health', setting out six principles including protecting human autonomy, ensuring transparency and fostering accountability.

title: HIPAA health privacy rules
text: The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), enacted in 1996, sets US rules for the privacy and security of protected health information held by covered entities such as hospitals, clinics and insurers.

title: Mailchimp: a bootstrapped exit
text: Email marketing company Mailchimp grew for about two decades without venture capital and was acquired by Intuit in 2021 in a deal valued at roughly 12 billion US dollars.

title: NASA Mars mission schedule
text: NASA mission schedule: the agency's next Mars mission, announced in January 2025, is scheduled to launch in early 2026 (first quarter). It is an orbiter mission focused on the Martian upper atmosphere and space weather.

title: Mars Sample Return delayed and restructured
text: NASA's Mars Sample Return campaign has been delayed and restructured. An independent review found the original plan could cost up to 11 billion US dollars with no return before 2040; in January 2025 NASA said it would choose between two cheaper landing architectures, with samples reaching Earth no earlier than the mid-2030s, and the FY2026 budget request proposed cancelling the program.

title: Perseverance rover landing
text: NASA's Perseverance rover landed in Jezero Crater on Mars on 18 February 2021. It is drilling rock cores and sealing them in sample tubes for possible future return to Earth.

title: Ingenuity helicopter mission ends
text: NASA's Ingenuity Mars helicopter ended its mission in January 2024 after damaging a rotor blade, having completed 72 flights in nearly three years, far beyond the five test flights originally planned. It no longer flies.

title: Earth-Mars distance and travel time
text: The distance between Earth and Mars ranges from roughly 55 million km at the closest approaches to about 400 million km when the planets are on opposite sides of the Sun. Typical transfer flights take six to nine months.

title: Opportunity rover mission
text: NASA's Opportunity rover landed in January 2004 on a planned 90-day mission and operated until a planet-encircling dust storm in June 2018; NASA declared the mission complete in February 2019.

title: Artemis I lunar test flight
text: Artemis I, the first flight of NASA's Space Launch System rocket, sent an uncrewed Orion capsule around the Moon between November and December 2022 as a test ahead of crewed Artemis missions.

title: Starship development milestones
text: SpaceX's Starship, the largest and most powerful rocket ever flown, made its first integrated test flight in April 2023. In October 2024 its Super Heavy booster was caught by the launch tower's mechanical arms for the first time.

title: First landing of an orbital-class booster
text: On 21 December 2015 SpaceX landed the first stage of a Falcon 9 back at Cape Canaveral after it helped deliver 11 satellites to orbit, the first time an orbital-class rocket booster had landed intact.

title: Size of the global space economy
text: The global space economy was worth about 570 billion US dollars in 2023, up roughly 7% from 2022, with commercial revenues accounting for close to 80% of the total and government budgets for the rest.

title: Countries that have soft-landed on the Moon
text: Five countries have achieved a soft landing on the Moon: the Soviet Union and the United States (both 1966), China (2013), India with Chandrayaan-3 near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, and Japan with its SLIM lander on 19 January 2024.

title: ISS retirement plan
text: NASA and its partners plan to operate the International Space Station through 2030 and then deorbit it using a dedicated US Deorbit Vehicle; in June 2024 NASA selected SpaceX to build that vehicle.

title: Bitcoin passes 100,000 dollars
text: Bitcoin traded above 100,000 US dollars for the first time on 5 December 2024, following a rally after the US presidential election.

title: Bitcoin price in 2025
text: Bitcoin set a new all-time high of roughly 126,000 US dollars in early October 2025 before a sharp pullback in the following weeks.

title: Spot bitcoin ETFs approved
text: The US Securities and Exchange Commission approved the first spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds on 10 January 2024, opening the asset to mainstream brokerage accounts.

title: Netflix paid memberships at end of 2024
text: Netflix ended 2024 with 301.6 million paid memberships worldwide after adding 18.9 million in the fourth quarter. From 2025 the company stopped reporting quarterly membership numbers.

title: Original iPhone launch
text: Apple's original iPhone was unveiled by Steve Jobs at Macworld in January 2007 and went on sale in the United States on 29 June 2007.

title: YouTube founding
text: YouTube was founded in February 2005 by Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim; the first video, 'Me at the zoo', was uploaded on 23 April 2005.

title: The ten-percent-of-the-brain myth
text: The claim that humans use only 10% of their brains is a myth. Brain imaging shows activity across virtually all brain regions over the course of a day, and damage to almost any area produces some deficit.

title: Facebook monthly active users
text: Meta reported that Facebook had about 3.07 billion monthly active users in the fourth quarter of 2023. Facebook first passed 2 billion monthly users in mid-2017.

title: The eight-second attention span claim
text: The widely repeated statistic that the average human attention span has fallen to eight seconds, shorter than a goldfish's nine, traces to a 2015 marketing report that cited a secondary website. Researchers have found no study supporting either number, and attention varies with the task.

title: Spotify user base
text: Spotify reported 675 million monthly active users and 263 million premium subscribers at the end of 2024.

title: Origins of the World Wide Web
text: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN in March 1989; the first web server and browser were running at CERN by the end of 1990, and CERN released the web software into the public domain in April 1993.

title: Netflix paid sharing
text: Netflix began charging US members an extra fee to share accounts with people outside their household in May 2023, after earlier tests in Latin America.

title: Netflix ad-supported plan launch
text: Netflix launched its lower-priced 'Basic with Ads' plan in 12 countries in November 2022, including the United States on 3 November 2022.

title: Netflix ad tier audience
text: Netflix said its ad-supported plan reached 94 million monthly active users globally in May 2025, up from 70 million in November 2024 and about 5 million in May 2023.

title: Global electric car sales 2024
text: Global electric car sales exceeded 17 million in 2024, more than 20% of all new cars sold worldwide. China accounted for nearly two-thirds of the total.

title: Norway EV market share
text: Battery-electric cars made up 88.9% of new passenger car registrations in Norway in 2024, the highest share of any country.

title: EV battery longevity
text: Most EV makers warranty traction batteries for at least 8 years or 100,000 miles. Fleet telematics analyses put average battery capacity loss at under 2% per year, implying useful lives well beyond the warranty period.

title: End of US federal EV tax credit
text: The US federal clean vehicle tax credit of up to 7,500 US dollars for new electric vehicles ended for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025.

title: What causes delayed muscle soreness
text: Delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), which peaks 24 to 72 hours after unfamiliar or eccentric exercise, is attributed to microscopic muscle damage and inflammation. Blood lactate returns to resting levels within about an hour after exercise, so lactic acid does not cause next-day soreness.

title: Men's marathon world record
text: Kelvin Kiptum set the men's marathon world record of 2:00:35 at the Chicago Marathon on 8 October 2023, breaking Eliud Kipchoge's 2:01:09 from Berlin in 2022. World Athletics ratified the record in February 2024.

title: Adult sleep recommendation
text: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine recommends that adults get seven or more hours of sleep per night on a regular basis to promote optimal health.

title: Colonial Pipeline ransomware attack
text: A ransomware attack in May 2021 led Colonial Pipeline, operator of the largest refined-fuel pipeline in the US, to halt operations for several days. The company paid a ransom of 75 bitcoin, then worth about 4.4 million US dollars, of which the Justice Department later recovered about 2.3 million.

title: Ransomware payment totals
text: Ransomware payments tracked on-chain hit a record of about 1.1 billion US dollars in 2023, then fell roughly 35% to about 814 million US dollars in 2024 as more victims refused to pay and law enforcement disrupted major groups.

title: Average cost of a data breach
text: The 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report put the global average cost of a breach at 4.44 million US dollars, down from a record 4.88 million in the 2024 report, the first decline in five years.

title: WannaCry outbreak
text: The WannaCry ransomware worm spread in May 2017, infecting more than 200,000 computers in about 150 countries and disrupting parts of the UK's National Health Service.

title: Daily water needs
text: The US National Academies set adequate total water intake at about 3.7 litres a day for men and 2.7 litres for women, counting water from all beverages and food. The popular 'eight glasses of water a day' rule has no specific scientific basis.

title: IARC classification of processed and red meat
text: In October 2015 the World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer classified processed meat as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1) and red meat as probably carcinogenic (Group 2A). The groups reflect strength of evidence, not degree of risk.

title: Added sugars on the Nutrition Facts label
text: The FDA's updated Nutrition Facts label, finalized in 2016, requires 'Added Sugars' to be listed in grams and as a percent Daily Value. Manufacturers with 10 million US dollars or more in annual food sales had to comply by 1 January 2020.

title: US e-commerce share of retail
text: E-commerce accounted for 16.4% of total US retail sales in the fourth quarter of 2024, on a seasonally adjusted basis.

title: Online cart abandonment rate
text: Across roughly 50 published studies, the average documented online shopping cart abandonment rate is about 70%. Extra costs at checkout and forced account creation are the most cited reasons.

title: Cyber Monday 2024 online spending
text: US online spending on Cyber Monday 2024 reached 13.3 billion US dollars, up 7.3% from the year before and the biggest online shopping day on record.

title: Amazon's origins
text: Amazon was founded by Jeff Bezos in July 1994 in Bellevue, Washington, and launched as an online bookstore in July 1995.

title: 2024 global temperature record
text: 2024 was the warmest calendar year on record and the first in which the global average surface temperature exceeded 1.5 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial level, at about 1.55 degrees Celsius according to the WMO.

title: Renewables share of global electricity
text: Renewable sources generated 32% of the world's electricity in 2024, and clean sources including nuclear passed 40%. Solar was the fastest-growing source of electricity for the 20th year in a row.

title: China's share of new solar capacity
text: China accounted for more than half of the world's newly installed solar photovoltaic capacity in both 2023 and 2024.

title: Atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration
text: The 2024 annual mean carbon dioxide concentration measured at Mauna Loa was about 424 parts per million, compared with roughly 315 ppm when measurements began in 1958 and about 350 ppm in the late 1980s.

title: Paris Agreement temperature goals
text: Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, countries agreed to hold the increase in global average temperature to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels and to pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees, measured as a long-term average.

title: TikTok reaches one billion users
text: TikTok said in September 2021 that it had passed 1 billion monthly active users worldwide.

title: Instagram monthly active users
text: Instagram passed 2 billion monthly active users in 2022, according to Meta. It had announced 1 billion monthly users in June 2018.

title: Facebook's founding
text: Facebook, originally 'TheFacebook', was launched by Mark Zuckerberg and classmates in February 2004 for Harvard students. It expanded to Stanford, Columbia and Yale in March 2004 and opened to the general public in September 2006.

title: Supreme Court TikTok ruling
text: In January 2025 the US Supreme Court upheld a federal law requiring ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations or face a ban in the United States.

title: Australia social media age limit
text: Australia passed a law in November 2024 requiring social media platforms to take reasonable steps to stop children under 16 from holding accounts, with enforcement starting in December 2025.

title: TSMC's share of advanced chipmaking
text: TSMC is the world's largest contract chipmaker and produces the large majority, commonly estimated at about 90%, of the world's most advanced leading-edge logic chips.

title: Moore's law
text: In 1965 Gordon Moore observed that the number of components on an integrated circuit was doubling every year. In 1975 he revised the forecast to a doubling roughly every two years, the version usually called Moore's law.

title: Global smartphone shipments 2024
text: Global smartphone shipments were about 1.24 billion units in 2024, up roughly 6% year over year and the first annual growth after two years of decline.

title: Nvidia market value
text: Nvidia became the first public company to reach a market value of 4 trillion US dollars in July 2025, about a year after it first passed 3 trillion in June 2024.

title: CHIPS and Science Act
text: The US CHIPS and Science Act, signed in August 2022, provides about 52.7 billion US dollars for domestic semiconductor manufacturing, research and workforce development.
